body.statement:
In the exact nested Gaussian score experiment, uniformly over every design satisfying the stated assumptions,
\[
 \frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}{8}\,
 \omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2
 \le R^{\star}
 \le \liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x\!\left[
   \{\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x)\}^2
 \right]
 \le \frac54\,\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2.
\]
body.justification: The field-level result is a global minimax MSE frontier for the causal terminal calendar ATT in the exact design-generated nested Gaussian experiment.
body.gap: General modulus theory supplies the shell after an operator is specified; it does not derive this staggered-DiD covariance or a valid scalar calendar reduction.
body.consumer: Compute \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) and the exposed affine rule to obtain a certified estimator and universal risk bracket.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(w(r)=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}total\text{-}modulus\text{-}rule}\), \(w\) is finite,
nondecreasing, and concave, and the canonical endpoints satisfy
\(x_r^+-x_r^-=h_r\) and
\(\ell(x_r^+)-\ell(x_r^-)=w(r)\).  We first verify that radius one belongs
to \(\mathcal R_+\).  Let \(e=(\mathbf 1_T,0)\).  Adding a scalar multiple
of \(e\) to an element of \(2\mathcal M_{T,m}\) preserves all Holder
difference inequalities, all bounds on the deviation coordinates, and all
calendar-centering equalities, by
\(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\).  Moreover,
\(\ell(e)=1\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}functional}\), while
\(Ke=\mathbf 1_O\ne0\) by
\(\mathrm{def{:}observation\text{-}operator}\).  The set \(O\) is nonempty
by \(\mathrm{ass{:}index\text{-}range}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}terminal\text{-}range}\).  If the maximizer \(h_1\)
had \(\|Kh_1\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}<1\), continuity of the norm
would therefore make \(h_1+a e\) feasible for all sufficiently small
\(a>0\), although \(\ell(h_1+a e)=\ell(h_1)+a\), a contradiction.
Consequently \(\|Kh_1\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}=1\).

The same constant direction gives
\[
 w(r)\ge
 \frac{r}{\|\mathbf 1_O\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}},
 \qquad r>0,
\]
so \(w\) is unbounded.  If its nonnegative right derivative at any positive
radius were zero, concavity would force every subsequent secant slope to be
nonpositive; monotonicity would then make \(w\) constant thereafter.  This
would contradict the preceding display.  Hence
\(s:=w'_+(1)>0\), and radius one is in \(\mathcal R_+\).

The supergradient inequality at one, evaluated at zero, gives
\(w(0)\le w(1)-s\).  Since \(w(0)\ge0\),
\[
 0\le b:=\frac{w(1)-s}{2}\le\frac{w(1)}2,
 \qquad 0<s\le w(1).
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}total\text{-}modulus\text{-}rule}\), \(b\) is the
maximal absolute bias of \(\widehat\theta_1\), and its standard deviation is
\(s\).  Therefore
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x[(\widehat\theta_1-\ell(x))^2]
 \le b^2+s^2\le\frac54w(1)^2.
\]
The defining inequality for \(r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}\) now yields
\[
 \liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_x
 \mathbb E_x[
   \{\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x)\}^2
 ]
 \le \inf_{r\in\mathcal R_+}(b_r^2+s_r^2)
 \le \frac54w(1)^2.
\]
Since \(R^\star\) is the infimum over all sample-measurable estimators by
\(\mathrm{def{:}risk\text{-}and\text{-}length}\), it is no larger than
each displayed worst-case risk and hence no larger than their lower limit.

For the converse, take the canonical endpoints \(x_1^-\) and \(x_1^+\).
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}score\text{-}covariance}\), their data laws
\(P_-\) and \(P_+\) are Gaussian with their common positive-definite
covariance \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\), mean difference \(Kh_1\), and target
separation \(\Delta=w(1)\).  If
\(d^2=\|Kh_1\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}^2\le1\), direct integration of
the Gaussian likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_+,P_-)
 =\mathbb E_-\!\left[
   \left\{\frac{dP_+}{dP_-}-1\right\}^2
 \right]
 =e^{d^2}-1\le e-1.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)=\frac12\mathbb E_-|dP_+/dP_--1|\)
therefore gives
\(\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\le\frac12\sqrt{e-1}\).

For an arbitrary estimator, decide for the endpoint whose target value is
closer to its reported value.  On either testing-error event the squared
estimation error is at least \(\Delta^2/4\).  The sum of the two testing-error
probabilities is at least \(1-\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\), by the defining
variational inequality for total variation.  Thus
\[
 \max_{\nu\in\{-,+\}}
 \mathbb E_\nu[(\widetilde\theta-\ell(x_1^\nu))^2]
 \ge \frac{\Delta^2}{8}
 \{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\}
 \ge
 \frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8w(1)^2.
\]
Both endpoints belong to \(\mathcal M_{T,m}\), so taking the infimum over
estimators proves the lower bound.  Every constant in the argument is
independent of \(N,T,m,q,L,B,\beta\), which proves the asserted uniformity.
